title.narrative: Output 7.1. Increased capacity of Member States to ensure respect for, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative:
In July 2022, the Government of Belize officially adopted and operationalized a comprehensive, integrated “Belize National Child Labour Policy and Strategy 2022-2025” which sets out priority areas, main outputs, timeline for implementation and responsibilities for the next four years, in line with the country longer term development framework. It was developed through an iterative process that included tripartite stakeholder inputs, and based on updated assessments of available empirical and qualitative information on the national child labour situation, including gender perspective which addresses the particular vulnerabilities of male and female children and adolescents in the determination of priority area, design of strategy and proposed interventions.
Throughout 2023, through implementation of activities identified in the policy, the Government mobilised social partners’ support and partnership for information campaigns and joint inspections in key rural areas and sectors, and improved the identification of and response to instances of child labour in Belize. They also improved the level of public awareness and understanding of child labour in high-risk communities. 1. ILO technical assistance advanced in Q3 2021 with the definition of suitable objectives and stakeholder consultations. In 2022, ILO collaborated with UNICEF and the Ministry of Rural Transformation to organise and facilitate nationwide consultations with public officials in various Ministries and agencies, trade unions, employers’ organisations, key civil society and NGO groups. The ILO orchestrated the procurement of key data processing equipment as part of institutional strengthening of the National Child Labour Tripartite Committee. ILO deployed technical expertise for detailed review of draft versions of the policy, providing recommendations, facilitation of validation workshops to finalize the document and support to edit and publish the formally approved policy and strategy document.
2. In 2023, the ILO provided advice on and facilitated Belize’s adhesion to the Regional Initiative Latin America and the Caribbean Free of Child Labour (RILAC), which gives the country access to opportunities for South-south cooperation and other support to implement the policy and strategy. The ILO also gave targeted assistance to the Ministry for implementation of a key public information and education campaign targeting education stakeholders, students and families in high-risk communities, in accordance with plans set out in the policy. ILO is providing ongoing support to the child labour committee to bolster monitoring of implementation.
